The girl asked whether the old letters had any mistakes, and Hollis said that the spelling was often inconsistent, that the same word might appear three ways on one page, and that the plural forms in particular followed no rule he could name. What interested him was the syntax, the way a sentence could wander for half a line before finding its verb, and the vocabulary, which was full of words for tools and weather that had since fallen out of use. He said that a language is not a fixed thing but a habit that shifts with every generation, and that the record of those shifts is kept not by the people who lived through them but by the paper they left behind.
